doc.name: A — leather goods catalogue, desert rock, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: bifold vegetable-tanned wallet
Category: leather goods
Shot programme: desert rock
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the still-life director on a commercial leather goods shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the low-angle monument in a desert rock treatment.

SUBJECT. A bifold vegetable-tanned wallet. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Low angle looking up so the product reads as architecture against the backdrop. Shoot on a 20mm wide at f/2, framing for frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with LED tube accents in two contrasting hues placed in depth. Stage the product on or against wet terrazzo, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
